segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The alarm had fired repeatedly and the pattern in my head felt strong enough on its own, so I treated it as a nuisance.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant estimated the likelihood that the alarm was false from easily recalled prior nuisance alarms without checking current corroborating evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I was focused on the panel itself because it was the loudest thing in the room and did not pull up the quieter pressure trend until later.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The prominent audible and visual alarm captured attention while a less salient but relevant pressure trend was overlooked.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The recent four hours looked clean, so I took the stable handover at face value and wrote off the older unresolved drift note as old news.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant overweighted the most recent stable report relative to the older unresolved drift evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I ran the standard feed-increase sequence, the same steps I had done about a hundred times, without stopping to reconsider the abnormal precursor.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A highly practiced action sequence was executed automatically without adapting it to the abnormal conditions.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The alarm, temperature climb, and shimmer reminded me of a prior compressor surge, so my instinct was to pull that same response template despite the missing vibration signature.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: A superficially similar prior event was used as the diagnostic template despite the absence of a defining feature.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The tube-rupture incident felt like the more likely explanation because it was dramatic and people brought it up in every shift briefing.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The likelihood of a rare failure mode was increased because the memorable incident was socially and mentally available.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: I went with the first checklist option that looked workable and did not compare it with the rest because I needed something fast.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Under a closing time window, the participant selected the first adequate option rather than evaluating all alternatives.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: The selected action stabilized the immediate trend, but a later review found another checklist step that would have addressed the underlying issue better.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: This is a substantive retrospective outcome assessment without an intentionally embedded hidden bias instance.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Phase 1: initial classification of the feed-heater high-temperature alarm
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The operator judged the current alarm likely false from the ease of recalling frequent recent nuisance alarms, without checking the log or the concurrent pressure trend.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is an established equivalent of Availability Bias here; both name likelihood/frequency judgment from easy recall.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: Frequent recalled nuisance alarms substituted for checking current evidence, affecting alarm-cause probability estimation.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Both verbatim quotes are present and directly support the frequency-of-recall mechanism. The later heat shimmer is hindsight and does not alter this first-decision match.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Phase 1: attention allocation between the annunciator and pressure-differential trend
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The visually and audibly prominent alarm drew attention away from a less prominent but relevant pressure-differential trend.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The candidate explicitly names Salience Bias as an alternative label, matching the target.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: It captures salience-driven attention allocation away from the quiet but diagnostically relevant pressure trend.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The supporting quotation is verbatim and maps to the segment's primary mechanism. The candidate appropriately notes the plausible normal-triage interpretation, but the hidden manifest establishes this occurrence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Phase 2: handover stability assessment versus unresolved older heater-duty drift
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The recent stable handover was overweighted relative to an older unresolved drift entry, which was discounted because of age without checking whether it had stopped.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The primary RAG label is the exact hidden target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The analysis identifies temporal weighting of the recent clean report over older unresolved evidence.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The two verbatim quotations are present and directly establish the stated age-based discounting. Later temperature rise is counterevidence, not evidence available during the handover judgment.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Phase 2: execution of the routine feed-increase sequence despite abnormal precursors
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A frequently practiced feed-increase sequence was executed automatically without adapting it to abnormal alarm and unresolved-drift conditions; the target is habitual action intrusion, not merely a deliberate judgment error.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Normalcy bias/default bias are near neighbors, not approved equivalents of Habit Intrusion. The alternative phrase 'Habitual responding' describes the behavior but is not established strongly enough here as an alternate target label.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The candidate captures automatic execution of a well-practiced sequence despite abnormal precursors, matching the distinctive action-execution mechanism.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: The quoted statement is verbatim and supports the automatic habitual sequence. It is a mechanism-first match only; strict label matching is not granted.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Phase 3: diagnostic pattern matching after the heat-shimmer report
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A response template from a superficially similar compressor-surge event was applied despite the absence of its distinguishing vibration signature.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Representativeness heuristic is an established equivalent for this similarity-based categorization: the RAG also names 'Similarity heuristic' as an alternative, and the mechanism is template transfer from surface resemblance.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: It identifies the superficial match to the remembered surge case and the unchecked absence of a defining feature.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Both quotations are verbatim and support the mechanism. The missing vibration signature is explicitly recognized retrospectively, but the participant says it was not checked before leaning on the template.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Phase 3: likelihood judgment about the memorable feed-heater tube-rupture incident
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: The likelihood of a rare tube-rupture cause was elevated by the vividness and repeated discussion of a past incident despite absent diagnostic markers.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is an established equivalent of Availability Bias, and the stated mechanism is vividness-driven likelihood judgment.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The analysis distinguishes vividness and repeated discussion from actual diagnostic markers, matching the target's availability mechanism.

Availability is detected twice with the two distinct intended mechanisms: recalled frequency at the alarm and vividness at tube-rupture likelihood judgment.
No quotes are fabricated, the summary counts are consistent, and the run makes no unsupported retrieval-support claim.

Candidate inclusion raises segment detection to 7/7 and mechanism-first recall to 7/7, while strict recall reaches 6/7 with two candidate-tier false positives.
